advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the fake `exists` in `_win_pin` case-insensitive (e.g. compare `ntpath.normcase` forms) so the `under-cwd-case` param actually exercises `_is_within`'s `normcase`
evidence: diff: `exists=lambda p: p in _WIN_EXISTING or p.startswith(_WIN_REPO),`

diff: `pytest.param(["-q", "d:\\A\\Rebar\\rebar\\tests\\unit\\test_x.py"], id="under-cwd-case"),` — `"d:\\A\\Rebar...".startswith("D:\\a\\rebar\\rebar")` is False and the path is not in `_WIN_EXISTING`
tests/_nested_pytest.py:111: `if arg.startswith("-") or not pathmod.isabs(path) or not exists(path):` — `continue` runs before `_is_within` (line 113) is reached
tests/_nested_pytest.py:73: `path, base = pathmod.normcase(path), pathmod.normcase(base)` — the behaviour this case claims to cover
advisory.finding: The `under-cwd-case` test case never reaches `_is_within`. The fake `exists` lambda is case-sensitive (`p.startswith(_WIN_REPO)`), so it returns False for the lowercased path. The argument is skipped as 'missing' and the result is `[]` either way. Removing `normcase` from `_is_within` would not fail this test.
scenarios: Someone drops `normcase` from `_is_within`. On Windows a test file under the repo with a different-case drive letter then gets pinned to its own directory, and this test still passes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip the value token after a separate-form path-valued pytest option (or restrict path detection to args not preceded by such an option), or narrow the docstring's mirror claim
evidence: tests/_nested_pytest.py:109-115: `for arg in args: path = arg.split("::", 1)[0]; if arg.startswith("-") or not pathmod.isabs(path) or not exists(path): continue; if _is_within(path, base, pathmod): return []; dirs.append(...)` — only the option token itself is skipped, not the value that follows it
tests/_nested_pytest.py:100-101: docstring: `Path arguments are picked the way pytest's get_dirs_from_args picks them: each non-option argument...`
test `test_an_option_value_that_is_not_a_path_is_ignored` only covers values that are not absolute (`-k`, `-p`), so nothing tests an absolute existing option value
advisory.finding: `_rootdir_pin` scans raw argv, so the value of a known option passed as a separate token (e.g. `--ignore C:\abs\dir`, `--deselect C:\abs\t.py::x`, `--log-file C:\abs\out`) is treated as a test path if it is absolute and exists. pytest's `get_dirs_from_args` only sees positional and unknown args after argparse has removed known options' values. So the docstring's claim to mirror pytest is wrong here. Such a value either suppresses the pin (if it is under cwd) or widens the pinned rootdir (if it is outside cwd).
scenarios: On Windows: `run_nested_pytest(tmp, '--ignore', str(REPO_ROOT/'tests'/'x'), str(tmp_test))` returns `[]` early, the pin is lost, and the %TEMP% collection race comes back.
`--deselect C:\other\t.py::x` together with a test under %TEMP%: commonpath widens the rootdir to `C:\`, so collection walks %TEMP% again.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip the pin when a pytest config file or setup.py exists in an ancestor of the path arguments, or document that the pin overrides config-derived rootdirs
evidence: tests/_nested_pytest.py:90: `With no ini file, pytest roots the session at the common ancestor of the cwd and the arguments' directories`
tests/_nested_pytest.py:105-106: `if any(_pins_rootdir(arg) for arg in args): return []` — only explicit flags are checked; nothing checks for a config file found by pytest itself
tests/_nested_pytest.py:62-63: `_ROOTDIR_OPTIONS = ("--rootdir", "--config-file", "--confcutdir")`

tests/unit/test_pytest_interleaved_conftest_args.py:46: `_write(root / "pytest.ini", "[pytest]\n")` shows callers already build tmp projects with ini files (that caller uses relative args, so it is not affected today)
advisory.finding: The pin is added even when pytest would find a config file (pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg) or a setup.py in the test path's ancestors. In that case pytest uses the config's directory as rootdir; an explicit `--rootdir` overrides that on every OS, including POSIX. The docstring scopes the problem to 'With no ini file', but the code never checks that condition. Only the `-c`/`--config-file` flags are treated as 'caller chose'.
scenarios: A caller builds `tmp/project/pytest.ini` and runs an absolute `tmp/project/tests/test_x.py` from the default cwd (REPO_ROOT). Before this change the rootdir was `tmp/project`; now it is `tmp/project/tests`, so nodeids and rootdir-relative output change on Linux and macOS too.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_win_pin`'s fake `exists` case-insensitive (as Windows is) so `under-cwd-case` actually reaches `_is_within`'s normcase comparison
evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:187: `exists=lambda p: p in _WIN_EXISTING or p.startswith(_WIN_REPO),`
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:218: `pytest.param(["-q", "d:\\A\\Rebar\\rebar\\tests\\unit\\test_x.py"], id="under-cwd-case"),`
tests/_nested_pytest.py:111: `if arg.startswith("-") or not pathmod.isabs(path) or not exists(path):` then `continue`, so `dirs` stays empty and the function returns `[]`
Inverted trace: remove `pathmod.normcase` from `_is_within` (tests/_nested_pytest.py:73) and this case still returns `[]` and passes
advisory.finding: The `under-cwd-case` parameter cannot catch a regression in the case-insensitive comparison it is meant to cover. The fake `exists` is case-sensitive, so the lowercased path is reported as missing and skipped before `_is_within` (and its `normcase`) is ever called.
scenarios: A refactor drops the normcase in `_is_within`. On real Windows, a caller passing `d:\a\rebar\rebar\tests\...` with cwd `D:\a\rebar\rebar` would get a wrong `--rootdir` pin, and this test would stay green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_win_pin`, use `exists=lambda p: ntpath.normcase(p) in {ntpath.normcase(e) for e in _WIN_EXISTING} or ntpath.normcase(p).startswith(ntpath.normcase(_WIN_REPO))`, so the lowercased under-cwd path counts as existing and the result depends on `_is_within`.

evidence: tests/_nested_pytest.py:113-114: `if _is_within(path, base, pathmod):` / `return []`
tests/_nested_pytest.py:88 docstring: "``["--rootdir", <dir>]`` when every path argument lies outside *cwd*, else ``[]``."
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:217: the only under-cwd case has a single path argument, so with `continue` instead of `return []` the empty `dirs` would still yield `[]`
No parameter combines an under-cwd argument with an outside-cwd argument
tests/_nested_pytest.py:119: `return ["--rootdir", pathmod.commonpath(dirs)]`
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:195-210 and 236-239: each positive case passes exactly one path argument
The only multi-path case (`two-drives`, line 227) covers the ValueError branch only
advisory.finding: Nothing tests the 'every path argument lies outside cwd' rule, i.e. that any argument under cwd suppresses the pin even when other arguments are outside it. The single-argument `under-cwd` case returns `[]` whether `_is_within` triggers `return []` or a `continue`.
merged_from: Combining several same-drive argument directories with `pathmod.commonpath(dirs)` is never tested with more than one directory. Every positive test passes a single path, so an implementation that returned `dirs[0]` would pass all of them.
scenarios: Named input: `_win_pin([f"{_WIN_REPO}\\tests\\unit\\test_x.py", _WIN_TEST])` should return `[]`. If the early return became `continue`, it would return `["--rootdir", _WIN_DIR]`, overriding pytest's rootdir for a mixed invocation, and every test would still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `pytest.param([f"{_WIN_REPO}\\tests\\unit\\test_x.py", _WIN_TEST], id="mixed-under-and-outside-cwd")` to the parametrize list of `test_the_pin_is_left_out_when_pytest_already_roots_the_session_correctly`.

evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:207: `_win_pin(["-k", "test_x or test_y", "-p", "no:randomly", _WIN_TEST])`
